recommendations.text: As the default strategy for patients with atrial fibrillation and CHA2DS2‑VASc score ≥1 in men and ≥2 in women, after up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy following the ACS event, dual antithrombotic therapy using a NOAC at the recommended dose for stroke prevention and a single oral antiplatelet agent (preferably clopidogrel) for up to 12 months is recommended.
recommendations.clinical_context: Patients with atrial fibrillation post-acute coronary syndrome (ACS)
recommendations.duration_and_drugs: Up to 1 week triple therapy then NOAC + single antiplatelet (preferably clopidogrel) for up to 12 months

recommendations.text: During PCI, a UFH bolus is recommended in any of the following circumstances: if the patient is on a NOAC; if the INR is <2.5 in VKA-treated patients.
recommendations.clinical_context: Periprocedural management during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)

content.notes: NOAC = non-vitamin K oral anticoagulant; VKA = vitamin K antagonist; UFH = unfractionated heparin; ACS = acute coronary syndrome; INR = international normalized ratio; CHA2DS2‑VASc = stroke risk score.
